body_lines: ## Why

Version-matched language guidance must come from the capability authority agents actually query. v0.5.0 delivers one independently accepted PHP navigation profile only after #477 proves built-in PHP behavior; unsupported or unmeasured ecosystem behavior remains an explicit abstention.

Today an agent approaching a PHP repository must infer which fallback summaries and relations are trustworthy. After this change, the installed ProjectAtlas skill leads the agent from ranked orientation through summaries and detailed graph evidence to exact slices, while stopping explicitly at dynamic, mixed, unsupported, or unmeasured behavior.
## What Changes
- Freeze PHP as the first v0.5 guidance profile after accepted built-in parser evidence.
- Generate guidance claims from the language registry, fixtures, representative repositories, and installed CLI/MCP behavior.
- Update only the version-matched ProjectAtlas plugin skill and generated support references.
- This scope supersedes the older incubation comment by selecting one exact first profile rather than a plural language campaign.
## Capabilities
- `repository-content-intelligence`: evidence-backed PHP navigation guidance with exact fallback and abstention boundaries.
## Architecture Diagrams
- [PHP language-guidance evidence flow](https://github.com/styler-ai/ProjectAtlas/blob/main/docs/v050-release-architecture.md#user-content-php-language-guidance-evidence-flow)
The view proves that installed guidance claims flow from accepted registry and representative behavior evidence before an agent receives a navigation route.
## Release Scope

Accepted for `v0.5.0-00` as one direct native sub-issue of release owner #492. Direct blockers: #477. It directly unlocks #490. #492 owns hierarchy visibility and progress, remains directly blocked by this issue, performs no feature or bug implementation, and closes last.
## Acceptance Criteria

- The installed version-matched guidance routes PHP agents through ranked orientation, summaries, detailed graph evidence, and exact slices, and every claim matches the accepted registry, fixtures, and representative repositories.
- Malformed, mixed HTML/PHP, dynamic, unsupported, and generated-source cases expose typed fallback or abstention without invented framework or relation claims.
- CLI, MCP, generated support references, and the packaged skill agree on version and capability truth while non-PHP guidance remains unchanged.
- When evidence does not support a PHP guidance claim, the profile omits or weakens that claim instead of expanding into a generic language-guidance framework.
## Non-Goals
- A plural language campaign.
- Framework or dynamic-resolution inference without evidence.
- Hand-written duplication of `LANGUAGE_CAPABILITIES`.
## Pre-Mortem
Likely failure modes:
- Guidance ships before #477 or drifts from the installed registry, so agents trust unsupported syntax or relations.
- A representative happy path is generalized into framework or dynamic-resolution claims without evidence.
Mitigations:
- [ ] Block guidance on accepted #477 evidence and derive every claim from the installed registry, fixtures, representative repositories, and compatibility tests. (OpenSpec tasks: 3.1, 3.2, 3.3)
- [ ] Keep framework and dynamic-resolution behavior in explicit fallback or abstention unless representative evidence establishes the claim. (OpenSpec tasks: 3.1, 3.3, 3.4)
## OpenSpec Tasks

- [ ] 3.1 Freeze PHP as the v0.5 first guidance profile after #477 acceptance; derive its syntax, symbol, relation, provenance, fallback, and abstention claims from `LANGUAGE_CAPABILITIES`, generated language-support data, PHP fixtures, and representative PHP repositories.

- [ ] 3.2 Update only the version-matched ProjectAtlas plugin guidance and its generated support references to route PHP tasks through overview, folders, files, summary, outline, search, detailed graph evidence, and exact slice without adding a generic language-guidance framework.

- [ ] 3.3 Prove positive PHP navigation, malformed and mixed HTML/PHP fallback, unsupported/dynamic behavior, generated-source abstention, CLI/MCP parity, version match, and representative-repository task outcomes in the owning language compatibility and installed-skill tests.
- [ ] 3.4 Review the final implementation against the architecture diagrams, update the diagrams or implementation until they agree, or reconfirm the reasoned N/A.
## Why

An agent asking why a symbol or file is relevant depends on the summary's reverse-caller context, but the current `load_import_relations_for_symbols -> import_alias_map -> called_by_map` path performs storage-hot alias and call-target work whose intended-scale behavior has not been measured. A faster-looking query that drops aliases, invents callers, or lets a global limit starve later targets would make navigation less trustworthy.

The issue therefore changes the decision workflow, not performance by assumption: measure the current path, compare one smallest shared service/database candidate, and adopt it only if representative evidence clears a frozen material threshold; otherwise retain current behavior with honest no-change evidence.
## What Changes
- Benchmark the exact current service/database hot path with real query plans and intended-scale fixtures.

- Compare only the smallest shared service/database candidate while preserving exact identity, language aliases, ambiguity rejection, per-target fairness, deterministic ordering, freshness, cancellation, bounded output, and all-or-error SQLite behavior.
- Adopt the measured winner or record a valid no-change outcome.
## Capabilities
- `repository-analysis-and-scale`: bounded deterministic reverse-caller summaries at representative scale.
## Architecture Diagrams
- [Reverse-caller query and decision boundary](https://github.com/styler-ai/ProjectAtlas/blob/main/docs/v050-release-architecture.md#user-content-reverse-caller-query-and-decision-boundary)
The view proves the existing storage-to-service ownership, the measured adoption/no-change fork, and the compatibility checks that bound either outcome.
## Release Scope

Accepted for `v0.5.0-00` as one direct native sub-issue of release owner #492. Direct blockers: #476, #480, #488, which first stabilize identity admission, bounded document publication, and durable module ownership so this benchmark measures the accepted shared path instead of moving foundations. It directly unlocks #490. #492 owns hierarchy visibility and progress, remains directly blocked by this issue, performs no feature or bug implementation, and closes last.
## Acceptance Criteria
- Representative SQLite benchmarks and query plans produce a reproducible threshold-based decision: adopt a material shared-path improvement or retain the current path with honest no-change evidence.
- Exact symbol identity, Rust/TypeScript/Python aliases, ambiguity rejection, per-target fairness, ordering, truncation, freshness, cancellation, and all-or-error failure behavior remain compatible.
- High-symbol, high-import, duplicate-alias, large, and corrupt-row cases remain bounded and never return false or partially decoded callers.
- No cache, substring shortcut, new analysis framework, or unmeasured performance claim is introduced.
## Non-Goals
- A speculative cache or new analysis framework.
- Substring matching that weakens caller correctness.
- A performance claim based only on tiny fixtures.
## Pre-Mortem
Likely failure modes:
- A faster query drops valid aliases, creates false callers, or starves later targets behind a global limit.
- Tiny fixtures hide table scans, allocation growth, or per-symbol work that dominates large summaries.
Mitigations:
- [ ] Compare candidates under the exact identity, alias, ambiguity, fairness, ordering, freshness, cancellation, and failure contract before adopting a winner. (OpenSpec tasks: 4.1, 4.2, 4.3)
- [ ] Benchmark intended-scale SQLite fixtures with statement, row, byte, allocation, output, and query-plan evidence before deciding. (OpenSpec tasks: 4.1, 4.3, 4.4)
## OpenSpec Tasks

- [ ] 4.1 Benchmark the current `load_import_relations_for_symbols -> import_alias_map -> called_by_map` path on small, high-symbol, high-import, duplicate-alias, and large representative SQLite databases; record wall/CPU/RSS/allocations, statements/rows/bytes, `EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, and output bytes, and freeze a material-improvement threshold before changing code.

- [ ] 4.2 Compare the current path with the smallest shared candidate, preserving exact symbol identity, Rust/TypeScript/Python aliases, ambiguity rejection, per-target fairness, deterministic ordering, truncation, freshness, cancellation, and all-or-error SQLite failure behavior.

- [ ] 4.3 Adopt only the measured winner at the shared service/database boundary or retain current code with reproducible no-change evidence; run the existing alias unit/E2E checks plus negative, stale, duplicate, large, corrupt-row, bounded-output, and representative-plan checks.
- [ ] 4.4 Review the final implementation against the architecture diagrams, update the diagrams or implementation until they agree, or reconfirm the reasoned N/A.
## Why

Agents wait for scan or watch convergence before current summaries, symbols, and relations can be trusted. Indexing already uses bounded worker pools and an atomic SQLite publication boundary, but parsing, structural summaries, graph derivation, staging, publication, and cleanup are not measured as one process resource envelope; separate pool lifecycles can oversubscribe the same host or feed the single writer inefficiently.

The before-to-after contract is evidence-led: profile the complete current path, pass one explicit process budget through existing owners, compare reuse, batching, or one shared pool, and adopt only a representative end-to-end win. A clean no-change decision is valid when scheduling overhead or contention erases the benefit.
## What Changes
- Profile cold scan and watch across parsing, summaries, graph derivation, staging, publication, and cleanup.
- Pass one process-level budget through existing owners and compare reuse, batching, or one shared pool with the current lifecycle.
- Preserve exact graph digests, bounded intermediates, cancellation, atomic publication, and cross-platform behavior.
## Capabilities
- `repository-analysis-and-scale`: measured indexing parallelism under one explicit process budget.
## Architecture Diagrams

- [Graph-construction worker and publication ownership](https://github.com/styler-ai/ProjectAtlas/blob/main/docs/v050-release-architecture.md#user-content-graph-construction-worker-and-publication-ownership)
The view proves host-wide budget ownership from CPU work through the one SQLite publication transaction and the cancellation or rollback termination paths.
## Release Scope

Accepted for `v0.5.0-00` as one direct native sub-issue of release owner #492. Direct blockers: #476, #480, #488, which stabilize admission, publication, and module ownership before resource measurements select a concurrency shape. It directly unlocks #384, #456, #464, #490. #492 owns hierarchy visibility and progress, remains directly blocked by this issue, performs no feature or bug implementation, and closes last.
## Acceptance Criteria

- Cold scan and incremental watch measurements cover the full parse-to-publication path and report wall time, CPU, RSS, allocations, filesystem and SQLite work, transaction/WAL behavior, persistent bytes, cancellation, and graph digest.
- A shared process budget or pool change lands only when representative evidence proves a material win; otherwise current behavior remains with reproducible no-change evidence.
- Accepted behavior preserves exact graph equivalence, deterministic ordering, one-generation atomic publication, bounded intermediates, cancellation, rollback, and Windows/Linux/macOS compatibility.
- No nested per-stage pool, new concurrency framework, or throughput trade that weakens publication truth is accepted.
## Non-Goals
- Nested or per-stage pools without host-wide accounting.
- A new concurrency framework or crate.
- Trading generation atomicity for throughput.
## Pre-Mortem
Likely failure modes:
- A faster parser oversubscribes CPU, RSS, I/O, or the single SQLite writer through repeated pools.
- Parallel ordering changes identities or advertises a partial generation after cancellation or failure.
Mitigations:
- [ ] Enforce one process-level worker budget and measure CPU, RSS, I/O, queues, and SQLite writer contention across all indexing stages. (OpenSpec tasks: 5.1, 5.2, 5.3)
- [ ] Assert exact graph digests, deterministic ordering, generation atomicity, cancellation, and rollback for every accepted parallel path. (OpenSpec tasks: 5.1, 5.3, 5.4)
## OpenSpec Tasks

- [ ] 5.1 Profile current cold scan and incremental watch across symbol parsing, structural summaries, graph derivation, staging, SQLite replacement, and cleanup on representative small/medium/large and high-edge repositories; record wall/CPU/RSS/allocations, filesystem bytes, rows, plans, transaction/WAL/checkpoint behavior, persistent bytes, cancellation, and exact graph digest.

- [ ] 5.2 Define one process-level indexing budget passed through existing `SymbolBuildOptions` and downstream stages; compare sequential reuse/batching or one shared Rayon pool with the current separate-pool lifecycle, including concurrent repositories and same-root writer contention.

- [ ] 5.3 Adopt only a measured improvement or retain current behavior; preserve exact graph equivalence, generation atomicity, deterministic ordering, bounded queues/intermediates, cancellation, late-failure cleanup, and Windows/Linux/macOS behavior.
- [ ] 5.4 Review the final implementation against the architecture diagrams, update the diagrams or implementation until they agree, or reconfirm the reasoned N/A.
## Why

The release workflow's `Filtered custom harness compatibility` step has no explicit bound even though neighboring release verification is bounded. The fix is the workflow-native timeout at that exact owner.
## What Changes
- Confirm the one reported workflow step and choose a value consistent with neighboring verification.
- Add only `timeout-minutes` while preserving the exact Cargo command and result.
- Extend the existing workflow-contract assertion. This v0.5 scheduling supersedes the old scheduling statement but preserves its deliberately narrow technical boundary.
## Capabilities
- `release-candidate-delivery`: deterministic failure for an overlong filtered custom-harness step.
## Architecture Diagrams
- [Filtered custom-harness timeout ownership](https://github.com/styler-ai/ProjectAtlas/blob/main/docs/v050-release-architecture.md#user-content-filtered-custom-harness-timeout-ownership)
## Release Scope

Accepted for `v0.5.0-00` as one direct native sub-issue of release owner #492. Direct blockers: none. #492 owns hierarchy visibility and progress, remains directly blocked by this issue, performs no feature or bug implementation, and closes last.
## Acceptance Criteria

- The exact `Filtered custom harness compatibility` release step has a workflow-native timeout consistent with neighboring verification while its Cargo command, output, exit status, and artifacts remain unchanged.
- An overlong invocation fails at that step instead of hanging release proof, without adding a child-process timeout wrapper.
- The existing workflow-contract assertion fails if the step name, command, or timeout drifts and unrelated jobs remain unchanged.
## Non-Goals
- A process-timeout wrapper.
- Inventorying or changing unrelated jobs.
- A new test or workflow framework.
## Pre-Mortem
Likely failure modes:
- The timeout lands at job scope or changes the Cargo command, masking the exact failing owner.
- The contract assertion checks only a name and allows the bound or command to drift.
Mitigations:
- [ ] Apply only the existing step-level timeout to the named release step while preserving the exact Cargo command and result. (OpenSpec tasks: 6.1, 6.2, 6.3)
- [ ] Lock the step name, command, and timeout together in the existing workflow-contract assertion. (OpenSpec tasks: 6.2, 6.3, 6.4)
## OpenSpec Tasks

- [ ] 6.1 Confirm `.github/workflows/release.yml` `Filtered custom harness compatibility` is the reported unbounded owner and select the existing step-level `timeout-minutes` mechanism and value consistent with neighboring release verification steps.
- [ ] 6.2 Add only that step timeout, preserving the exact Cargo command, output, exit status, and workflow artifacts; do not add a timeout wrapper or child-process framework.
- [ ] 6.3 Extend the existing workflow-contract assertion to cover the step name, command, and timeout and run the locked YAML/parser, targeted Cargo test, and workflow/IssueOps checks.
- [ ] 6.4 Review the final implementation against the architecture diagrams, update the diagrams or implementation until they agree, or reconfirm the reasoned N/A.
## Why

Current graph analysis cannot answer bounded reachability from an explicit set of entrypoints without overclaiming deletion safety. An agent must currently interpret generic neighborhoods and incomplete relation coverage by hand, which can turn absence of evidence into a false dead-code conclusion. v0.5.0 adds a non-persistent typed profile so the workflow becomes explicit entrypoints to bounded traversal to reachable, evidence-backed unreachable candidates, or inconclusive results with exact source evidence.
## What Changes
- Define exact anchors, admitted relation families, bounds, coverage prerequisites, and typed uncertainty.
- Reuse the normalized graph and existing bounded analysis service for node-simple reachability.
- Return exact source evidence and preserve wrong-root, stale, ambiguous, unsupported, truncated, and canceled outcomes.
## Capabilities
- `repository-analysis-and-scale`: bounded entrypoint-aware reachability with typed uncertainty.
## Architecture Diagrams
- [Entrypoint-profile reachability](https://github.com/styler-ai/ProjectAtlas/blob/main/docs/v050-release-architecture.md#user-content-entrypoint-profile-reachability)
The view proves exact anchor admission, bounded node-simple traversal, and the uncertainty paths that terminate without deletion authority.
## Release Scope

Accepted for `v0.5.0-00` as one direct native sub-issue of release owner #492. Direct blockers: #358, #477. It directly unlocks #490. #492 owns hierarchy visibility and progress, remains directly blocked by this issue, performs no feature or bug implementation, and closes last.
## Acceptance Criteria
- A valid bounded entrypoint profile returns deterministic reachable, evidence-backed unreachable-candidate, or inconclusive results with reusable exact source evidence.
- Empty, stale, wrong-root, ambiguous, unsupported, incomplete-coverage, over-budget, truncated, or canceled requests fail or remain inconclusive and never claim deletion safety.
- Cycles, disconnected graphs, multiple or duplicate anchors, dynamic uncertainty, and replay preserve node-simple bounds and CLI/MCP parity.
- Existing graph storage remains authoritative; no persisted profile, reachability table, or deletion command is added.
## Non-Goals
- A dead-code deletion command.
- Persisted profiles or reachability tables.
- Dynamic-language completeness claims.
## Pre-Mortem
Likely failure modes:
- Incomplete relations are presented as proof that code is dead.
- Cycles, duplicate anchors, or output truncation produce unstable or falsely complete results.
Mitigations:
- [ ] Return typed inconclusive results whenever relation coverage is incomplete and never present a reachability candidate as deletion authority. (OpenSpec tasks: 7.1, 7.2, 7.3)
- [ ] Cover cycles, duplicate or invalid anchors, truncation, cancellation, and deterministic replay through the owning analysis and adapter tests. (OpenSpec tasks: 7.1, 7.3, 7.4)
## OpenSpec Tasks

- [ ] 7.1 Define the non-persistent typed `EntrypointProfile` request contract, exact file/symbol anchors, supported resolved relation families, profile/input/output bounds, graph-coverage prerequisites, cursor binding, and typed uncertainty; reuse existing graph storage and reject empty, stale, wrong-root, ambiguous, unsupported, or over-budget profiles before traversal.

- [ ] 7.2 Extend the existing bounded analysis service with node-simple reachability from every accepted entrypoint and classify reachable, evidence-backed unreachable candidate, and inconclusive; adapters only decode/serialize the shared typed contract and never claim deletion safety.

- [ ] 7.3 Cover reachable, unreachable, cyclic, disconnected, multi-entrypoint, duplicate/invalid anchor, dynamic uncertainty, incomplete relation coverage, stale generation/cursor, truncation, cancellation, wrong root, deterministic replay, CLI/MCP parity, and representative Rust/PHP repository tasks with exact source evidence.
- [ ] 7.4 Review the final implementation against the architecture diagrams, update the diagrams or implementation until they agree, or reconfirm the reasoned N/A.
## Why

JavaScript ecosystem users need `npm install` to lead to the same verified native ProjectAtlas runtime and command behavior as every other installer, not to a JavaScript reimplementation or an apparently installed but unusable package. The intended workflow is package installation or explicit scripts-disabled materialization, exact tuple/version/digest verification, atomic cache activation, then transparent forwarding of the user's complete CLI or MCP process contract.
## What Changes
- Freeze package identity, supported Node/npm and platform tuples, provenance, digest, cache, offline, and lifecycle-script-disabled contracts.
- Implement the smallest wrapper around the existing verified native runtime.
- Preserve every CLI/MCP argument, stream, signal, exit, root, config, database, and format contract.
## Capabilities
- `cli-installation-surface`: integrity-checked npm materialization of the native ProjectAtlas runtime.
## Architecture Diagrams
- [npm runtime selection and integrity](https://github.com/styler-ai/ProjectAtlas/blob/main/docs/v050-release-architecture.md#user-content-npm-runtime-selection-and-integrity)
The view proves that npm owns only selection, verification, cache activation, and forwarding while the native runtime remains the sole product authority.
## Release Scope

Accepted for `v0.5.0-00` as one direct native sub-issue of release owner #492. Direct blocker: #491, which first freezes the complete short-command forwarding and process contract that npm must preserve instead of inventing an npm-specific CLI. #492 owns hierarchy visibility and progress, remains directly blocked by this issue, performs no feature or bug implementation, and closes last.
## Acceptance Criteria

- On each supported tuple, npm materializes and launches the exact release-version and SHA-256-verified native runtime while preserving all CLI/MCP arguments, streams, signals, exit codes, roots, configuration, database selection, and formats.
- Disabled lifecycle scripts have an explicit verified materialization route, and unsupported tuples, missing assets, offline misses, or version/digest mismatches refuse launch.
- Concurrent, interrupted, stale-cache, update, repair, and uninstall paths never activate a partial or wrong-tuple runtime and remove only owned state.
- `projectatlas` and the accepted `atlas` forwarding contract remain compatible; npm does not create a JavaScript runtime or npm-specific command behavior.
## Non-Goals
- A JavaScript reimplementation of ProjectAtlas.
- Launching an unverified or mismatched asset.
- An npm-specific CLI contract.
## Pre-Mortem
Likely failure modes:
- Lifecycle scripts are disabled and the package silently appears installed without a usable verified runtime.
- Concurrent or interrupted materialization activates a partial, stale, or wrong-tuple binary.
Mitigations:
- [ ] Provide an explicit verified materialization route when lifecycle scripts are disabled and refuse to expose an unverified runtime. (OpenSpec tasks: 8.1, 8.2, 8.3)
- [ ] Use process-safe locking, private staging, digest and tuple verification, atomic activation, cleanup, retry, and stale-cache repair. (OpenSpec tasks: 8.1, 8.2, 8.3, 8.4)
## OpenSpec Tasks

- [ ] 8.1 Define the npm package name/scope, supported npm and Node floor, registry-package and native-asset provenance, supported target tuple matrix, release-version and SHA-256 digest contract, install-time versus first-run materialization, package-manager-script-disabled behavior, proxy/offline behavior, process-safe cache locking and atomic activation, cache/update policy, and ownership across npm package, release assets, installers, and runtime. Add only repository artifacts justified by that boundary.

- [ ] 8.2 Package the smallest npm adapter that selects, stages, verifies, and atomically activates the matching existing native runtime, exposes an explicit materialization path when lifecycle scripts are disabled, and preserves CLI/MCP arguments, stdout, stderr, exit codes, signals, selected root/config/database, and machine formats.

- [ ] 8.3 Cover supported and unsupported tuples, missing or mismatched version/digest, disabled lifecycle scripts, proxy/offline/cache states, concurrent and interrupted materialization, stale cache repair, update, uninstall, and CLI/MCP smoke behavior on Windows, Linux, and macOS without launching or registering an unverified runtime.
- [ ] 8.4 Review the final implementation against the architecture diagrams, update the diagrams or implementation until they agree, or reconfirm the reasoned N/A.
## Why

Structurally valid generated files do not prove Claude Code or OpenCode will consume their paths, fields, version guards, or selected ProjectAtlas database. This is proof-gap hardening, not a claim that a current generated configuration has been reproduced as broken: v0.5.0 must exercise the actual installed host readers and establish a real ProjectAtlas MCP session from isolated configuration roots before compatibility is accepted.
## What Changes
- Trace the native config schemas, version/runtime/root fields, repair ownership, and restart behavior.
- Use each installed host's real configuration reader, then initialize MCP and read bounded ProjectAtlas source evidence.
- Cover invalid, stale, repaired, missing-host, shared-registry, explicit-root, and uninstall paths without touching unrelated host state.
## Capabilities
- `cli-installation-surface`: real isolated host consumption of installer-generated ProjectAtlas configuration.
## Architecture Diagrams
- [Real host configuration consumption](https://github.com/styler-ai/ProjectAtlas/blob/main/docs/v050-release-architecture.md#user-content-real-host-configuration-consumption)
The view proves the boundary from installer-owned files through each real host reader to MCP initialization and exact source-evidence readback, including fail-closed isolation.
## Release Scope

Accepted for `v0.5.0-00` as one direct native sub-issue of release owner #492. Direct blockers: #491. #492 owns hierarchy visibility and progress, remains directly blocked by this issue, performs no feature or bug implementation, and closes last.
## Acceptance Criteria

- Each installed supported host consumes its installer-generated configuration through the real host reader, establishes MCP, and returns bounded ProjectAtlas source evidence from the exact selected runtime, version, database, and project route.

- Invalid, stale, wrong-version, missing-host, shared-registry, explicit-root, repaired, and uninstall paths return the owned failure or recovery outcome without falling back to checked-in or ambient state.
- Isolated home and configuration roots prevent credentials, authentication, unrelated global configuration, or project data from being read or mutated by the proof.
- If current generated configurations already satisfy both real host readers, the issue may close with reproducible no-product-change evidence rather than inventing a failure.
## Non-Goals
- Parser-only proof of host configuration.
- Using a checked-in fallback as installed proof.
- Mutating credentials, authentication, unrelated global config, or project data.
## Pre-Mortem
Likely failure modes:
- A generated file parses in tests but the real host ignores its path, fields, or version guard.
- The E2E passes by reading ambient host state or a different global ProjectAtlas registration.
Mitigations:
- [ ] Exercise each generated configuration through the actual supported host reader and establish a real MCP session with source-evidence readback. (OpenSpec tasks: 9.1, 9.2, 9.3)
- [ ] Isolate home and configuration roots and assert the exact runtime, database, version, and project route so ambient state cannot satisfy the proof. (OpenSpec tasks: 9.1, 9.3, 9.4)
## OpenSpec Tasks

- [ ] 9.1 Trace installer-generated Claude Code and OpenCode configuration ownership, native schemas, absolute runtime/database/config fields, version guards, restart messaging, isolated host roots, and collision-safe repair paths.

- [ ] 9.2 Make each installed host consume its generated configuration through the real host reader and establish a ProjectAtlas MCP session without weakening per-project routing or treating structural parsing or checked-in fallback state as proof.

- [ ] 9.3 Exercise installer-generated Claude Code and OpenCode configuration through the actual installed host readers in isolated homes/config roots on supported platforms. Cover valid launch and MCP initialize/session/source-evidence readback; missing host; invalid, stale, wrong-version, and repaired configuration; shared-registry default versus explicit project-root routing; and uninstall. Do not mutate unrelated host-global configuration, credentials, authentication state, or project data.
- [ ] 9.4 Review the final implementation against the architecture diagrams, update the diagrams or implementation until they agree, or reconfirm the reasoned N/A.
## Why

A clean ProjectAtlas user currently pays normal initialization and scan cost, a safe workflow whose current-source authority is already understood. A released-main database seed might shorten that path, but it also adds release bytes, revision and schema identity, migration, writable-copy, dirty-source refresh, rollback, and lifecycle obligations that can cost more than they save.

The intended before-to-after outcome is conditional: measure the complete user-visible and resource cost, then either retain normal initialization or activate an exact verified seed as a private writable starting point before normal current-source reconciliation. A seed is not the goal; net product benefit without weaker identity or recovery is.
## What Changes
- Measure normal initialization against an exact-revision seed across supported platforms and intended-scale resource dimensions.
- Only after a frozen net-benefit threshold wins, land the smallest database-first identity, integrity, migration, writable-copy, and fallback boundary.

- Preserve independent writable project state, current/dirty-source reconciliation, and safe full initialization. This v0.5 scope supersedes the old v0.5.2 scheduling comment while retaining its technical constraints.
## Capabilities
- `repository-analysis-and-scale`: evidence-led released-main database baseline decision with safe fallback.
## Architecture Diagrams
- [Released-main database baseline decision](https://github.com/styler-ai/ProjectAtlas/blob/main/docs/v050-release-architecture.md#user-content-released-main-database-baseline-decision)
The view proves the measured adoption/no-change fork and, only after adoption, the exact verification, private-copy, reconciliation, and full-init fallback boundary.
## Release Scope

Accepted for `v0.5.0-00` as one direct native sub-issue of release owner #492. Direct blockers: #358 supplies the accepted process resource model, #465 and #477 settle the v0.5 content/parser workload the baseline must represent, and #484 settles lossless worktree identity before a released database can be copied safely. It directly unlocks #490. #492 owns hierarchy visibility and progress, remains directly blocked by this issue, performs no feature or bug implementation, and closes last.
## Acceptance Criteria

- The seed decision measures normal initialization and an exact-revision baseline across startup, refresh, migration, release/download bytes, private-copy cost, CPU, RSS, I/O, WAL, and persistent storage against a frozen net-benefit threshold.
- If the threshold wins, activation verifies exact revision, schema, and digest, creates one private writable project copy, and reconciles current and dirty source before reporting readiness.
- Wrong, corrupt, truncated, incompatible, canceled, or active-WAL input preserves authored state and safely falls back to normal full initialization without sharing writable state.
- If representative evidence does not prove net benefit, ProjectAtlas retains normal initialization with a reproducible no-product-change decision.
## Non-Goals
- Shipping a seed without net product benefit.
- Sharing one writable released database across projects.
- Bypassing schema, revision, digest, freshness, or authored-state checks.
## Pre-Mortem
Likely failure modes:
- A seed improves a synthetic startup metric but increases release bytes, migration risk, or real refresh time.
- A copied database is treated as shared or current despite revision/schema/digest mismatch or dirty source.
Mitigations:
- [ ] Freeze a net-benefit threshold that includes release bytes, migration risk, writable-copy cost, and current-source refresh before accepting a seed. (OpenSpec tasks: 10.1, 10.2, 10.3)
- [ ] Verify revision, schema, and digest before creating a private writable copy, and fall back safely to full initialization on any mismatch. (OpenSpec tasks: 10.2, 10.3, 10.4)
## OpenSpec Tasks

- [ ] 10.1 Measure clean normal initialization and scan, database/startup/migration/freshness/update time, release/download/unpack bytes, private-copy activation, and intended-scale CPU/RSS/I/O/WAL/persistent bytes on exact representative revisions and supported platforms; freeze a net-benefit threshold.

- [ ] 10.2 Only if the threshold wins, design the private writable copy boundary and land the smallest database identity/schema/index/query/transaction/migration/integrity/rollback/fallback delta with real write/read, active-WAL, corrupt/truncated, wrong-revision, wrong-schema, and cancellation coverage before installer/service use.

- [ ] 10.3 Prove revision and digest identity, authored-state isolation, refresh to dirty/current source, update/repair/uninstall behavior, bounded release/write amplification, and safe full-init fallback, or retain normal database creation with reproducible no-change evidence.
- [ ] 10.4 Review the final implementation against the architecture diagrams, update the diagrams or implementation until they agree, or reconfirm the reasoned N/A.
## Why

Agents use architecture analysis to choose a coherent work area, but weak components often collapse a densely connected repository into one giant group and provide no useful orientation. v0.5.0 changes only the optional community answer: deterministic weighted label-propagation v1 groups the existing normalized evidence when it converges inside fixed bounds, otherwise reports typed uncertainty.
